title: Nammazhwar
body:
Nammazhwar

Forty-Three days had passed since Lord Sri Krishna had ascended to Sri Vaikuntham. A childless couple, Kari and Udayanangai, visited Tirukurungudi to pray for the birth of a child. It is said that they requested the Lord for a child who would be just like Him. As none in this universe is comparable to Him, it is noted that Nambi Himself reincarnated as Namazhwar. Thus, in the Vaikasi month under Visaka Nakshathram, Namazhwar was born. As soon as he was born, he exhibited very peculiar behavior in the form of not crying or suckling. The couple, out of concern, is said to have taken the baby to the Adinatha Perumal Temple to pray to the Lord for the baby's well-being. Namazhwar is also said to be an amshavataram of Sri  Vishwakshenar, who is said to be third in line in the Acharya Parampara after the Lord Sriman Narayana and Mahalakshmi Thayaar. The couple is said to have tied a cradle near the Tamarind tree that was present in the temple courtyard.

Divine Tamarind Tree

The baby is said to have crawled out of the cradle and into a small crater-like space within the tree, where it started a deep meditation. The baby is said to have stayed in this meditative state for sixteen years. At this time, Madurakavi Azhwar is said to have been at Ayodhya and offering argyam as per his Nityakarmam when he saw a blinding light at the edge of the horizon. Recognizing the meditative nature of the divine light is said to have started to follow the light. In pursuit of the light, Madurakavi Azhwar is said to have traveled south, crossing Tiruvenkatam, then Tiruvallikeni, then Sri Rangam, then Madurai, and finally, he reached Kurugur. When Madurakavi Azhwar reached the divine tree, he saw a child in a deep meditative state and was worried whether the child was still alive or not. Madurakavi Azhwar is said to have thrown a rock near the boy to test his consciousness. When the boy opened his eyes, Madurakavi Azhwar was said to have asked a question, "Sethathin Vayatrill Siriyadhu Pirandhaal Yeththai Thindru Enge Kiddakum?" Madurakavi Azhwar was referring to the Jeevaathma. Madurakavi Azhwar asked When the jeevaathma enters a lifeless body, how would it survive? What would it feed on, and how would it survive? This is when Nammazhwar is said to have first spoken by saying, "Aththaith Thindru Ange Kidakkum.". Nammazhwar's reply said that the lifeless body would experience the pleasures and pains of life before attaining paramapadam or moksham. Madurakavi Azhwar was so stunned by the boy's response that he begged to be his disciple. Madurakavi Azhwar composed 11 pasurams in praise of his Acharya, Swami Nammazhwar, known as Kanninun Shiruthambu, which are included among the 4000 Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
 
When Nammazhwar was ready to attain paramapadam, Madurakavi Azhwar asked Nammazhwar, full of tears, what to do next. Nammazhwar advised Madurakavi Azhwar to boil the waters of Tamraparni, and he said that an idol would form during the boiling of the water. Madurakavi Azhwar did as per Nammazhwar's advice. After boiling the waters of Tamraparni, he obtained an idol of Bhagavad Ramanuja. He was surprised to see that the idol was different from what he had expected. He went to Nammazhwar with the idol, and the latter told him that this idol was that of a Bhavishyadhacharya (Future Guru) and that he would be born 4000 years from then. He again advised boiling the waters of Tamraparni. Madurakavi Azhwar once again boiled the waters of Tamraparni and finally got the idol of Nammazhwar.
